title: Indian security forces neutralize senior Laskhar-E-Toiba Commander, Musa aka Asif Fauji, in an intelligence-led operation in J&K
subtitle:
Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place
Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces, is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the UT of J&K
With Musa’s killing, entire group of four senior LeT Commanders operating in J&K since 2022, and responsible for several sensational attacks, stands neutralized
Security Forces neutralized the three other members of the group in separate encounters of Junaid Bhat, Suleman and Yasir
Current encounter to neutralize Musa was part of an ongoing long-sustained ‘Operation Sheruwali’, started in May, 2026
body_text:
In an intelligence-led joint Security Forces operation, senior Lashkar-e-Toiba Commander, Musa aka Asif Fauji, was neutralized at Gurwatkalan, Khansahib PS of Budgam District, J&K. Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place after technical and human intelligence about his movement and presence were received.
Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the UT of J&K. With Musa’s killing, the entire group of four senior LeT Commanders operating in the UT since 2022, and responsible for sensational attacks, like Halan attack (Aug 2023), DKG attack (Dec 2023), Kandi attack (May 2023), Shahsitar attack (May 2024), Shiv Khori attack (June 2024), Gagangir attack (Oct 2024), Bootapathri attack (Oct 2024) and Baisaran attack (Apr 2025), stands neutralized. The three other members of the group were neutralized by Security Forces in separate encounters of Junaid Bhat (Dec 03, 2024, Dachigam), Suleman (July 28, 2025, OP Mahadev), and Yasir (Sep 04, 2026, Op Asdhar). The current encounter to neutralize Musa was part of an ongoing long-sustained operation.
Over the past few years, all security agencies—such as the Jammu & Kashmir Police, the Indian Army, and the CAPF—have been conducting counter-terrorism operations in close coordination, yielding positive results.
